extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (senior/key personnel) preparing biographical sketches and research support sections
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the NIH-format Biographical Sketch and Research Support information for Senior/Key Personnel on an NIH grant application (follow the specified section headings and page limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow this format; page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit mandatory formatting and length requirement for the Biographical Sketch; all the subsequent sections (A–D) should be presented in this format and fit within the five-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table with columns for Institution and Location, Degree (if applicable), Completion Date MM/YYYY, and Field of Study. Start with undergraduate (baccalaureate) and include all subsequent professional, residency, and postdoctoral training as applicable. Rows can be added or removed to reflect actual training history.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement (section header shown as 'A. Personal Statement')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise narrative describing the individual's relevant research focus, major accomplishments, qualifications for the proposed role, mentoring experience, and how their background supports the proposed project. Examples in the text: describe decades of work, major findings, mentoring record, and direct relevance to the applicant's proposal and mentorship capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions and Employment (list of prior and current positions with dates and titles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List employment history with dates and institutional affiliations (e.g., '2011-13 Excellence Fellow, Institute for Health... Rutgers University'). Include academic appointments, research positions, teaching positions, and other relevant employment. Present in reverse chronological or clearly dated order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Experience and Professional Memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Experience and Professional Memberships (section header appearing under Positions/Honors)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List professional society memberships, editorial/peer-review roles, ad hoc reviewer activities, advisory roles, and other professional service. Include timeframes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors (section header appearing in the biosketch)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List awards, fellowships, prizes, and honors with dates and awarding institutions (examples shown: 'Matilda White Riley Published Article Award', 'Harvard Medical School’s excellence in mentoring award').

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions to Science (numbered narrative descriptions of major research contributions with supporting citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize discrete thematic contributions (e.g., 'Identification of a New Mental Disorder – Prolonged Grief Disorder'; 'Scales to Measure Psychosocial Aspects of Oncology'). For each contribution provide a short explanatory paragraph and list representative publications supporting the contribution (numbered citations). Indicate the individual's role in the projects (e.g., lead, co-investigator, first-author) where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Publications / Bibliographic citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation lists accompanying Contributions to Science and elsewhere (numerical citations tied to contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full citation details (authors, title, journal, year, DOI or PMID/PMCID where available). Use these citations to illustrate and substantiate the described contributions to science.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Additional Information: Research Support and/or Scholastic Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Information: Research Support and/or Scholastic Performance (section header for ongoing and completed support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide entries for ongoing and completed research support. For each entry include grant number (if applicable), funding agency, project title, a brief statement of the major goal(s) of the project, the individual's role (e.g., PI, MPI, Co-I, Role: Postdoctoral Trainee), and project dates. Distinguish ongoing from completed support and include institutional or foundation awards as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support entry details (what to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research support entries should state the grant ID, funding source, project title, major goal(s), role of the person, and start/end dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'T32 AG049666 The Weill Cornell Medical College Research Training Program in Behavioral Geriatrics — The major goal of this grant is to train MD & PhD researchers... Role: Postdoctoral Trainee. Prigerson, Reid (PIs) 07/01/16 - 06/30/21.' Use similar concise descriptive language for each support item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of relevance/fit for mentoring and institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative justification of the institutional environment and mentor qualifications for the proposed award (e.g., 'Weill Cornell’s Division ... is an ideal environment for me to hold a K99/R00 award').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though presented as applicant narrative, the document demonstrates that a strong biosketch/application should describe (1) the mentor's credentials and prior relevant funding, (2) the institutional resources and environment (center, expertise) that support the candidate, and (3) how the mentor/center's expertise aligns with the proposed work. Include mentorship track record and examples of mentor's funded projects and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities in prior projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the individual's role in prior projects (e.g., 'lead on study design, data analysis, and manuscript preparation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing past work, explicitly state the person's responsibilities (lead investigator, co-investigator, research assistant) to clarify contributions and level of independence. Use these role statements to support the case for the candidate's qualifications.
